question: Does smooth log-spectrum compression find a better representation-conditioning point than cap-16 whitening, and is complete whitening useful when its weak-direction amplification is treated as intentional?

source.basis: the frozen factorized sequence/channel basis from regularized_whitening/selected_transform.pt
source.comparison: cap-16 common/uniform FID/KID-5k 88.5374/0.073375; unwhitened native v27 26.7430/0.017538

transform.formula: gain_j proportional to power_j^(-gamma/2), with one global scalar making mean transformed training power one
transform.resulting_spectrum: transformed power proportional to original power^(1-gamma)
transform.interpretation: gamma=0 is the rotation-only control; gamma=1 is complete whitening; intermediate gamma linearly compresses log eigenvalues without a hard threshold
transform.null_policy: Do not cap the full-whitening stress test. Report split stability and a float16 quantization-noise proxy for the weak tail. Stop an arm only for non-finite values or failure of the existing float32/float16/decode inversion gates.

analysis.fit_split: same first 25000 training examples as the frozen basis
measurements: complete transformed held-out covariance spectra and effective ranks
float32 and simulated-float16 inversion and decoded errors
fixed-basis power agreement between disjoint training halves
sequence-eigenspace principal overlap between disjoint training halves

training_screen.objective: common global time and uniform flow loss only
training_screen.reason: isolate basis rotation and smooth whitening strength before reintroducing beta timing or loss weights
training_screen.common_recipe: prior seed 1, width 512, depth 12, eight heads, QK RMS normalization, batch 256, 60000 steps, learning rate 1e-4, 1000 warmup, 50-step Heun evaluation seed 54321

selection.advance_to_10000: advance the best arm and any arm within two FID of it or with FID/KID disagreement
selection.schedule_followup: only the best healthy gamma may receive a later common-versus-beta timing comparison

gpu_protocol: /workspace/GPU_QUEUEING.md; every analysis, cache build, training run, and evaluation uses a lifetime gpu-claim and supervisor

analysis_result.verdict: All four training gammas are numerically healthy. The weak spectrum is exceptionally stable across data halves and remains far above the source-float16 quantization proxy. Proceed with the common-time/uniform-loss gamma screen, including intentional full whitening.
